name: Weaver 26" Leather Upper Climber Straps
title: Weaver Leather Upper Climber Straps, 26 Inch
meta: Weaver leather upper climber straps in a 26 inch length hold your spurs snug below the knee. Fit tips, break-in advice and when to replace worn straps.
tagline: Replacement 26 in leather upper straps that keep your spurs tight below the knee.
summary: Weaver leather upper climber straps are the 26 inch straps that wrap the calf just below the knee and hold the top of your spur shanks against your leg. When the old pair cracks, stretches or the holes tear out, a fresh set brings back a solid, stable gaff.
highlights: 26 in upper (calf) straps for tree climbers
Leather construction from Weaver Leather
Holds the shank tight so the gaff bites cleanly
Replaces stretched, cracked or torn straps
Sold for use with climber pads and lower straps

p: On spurs, the upper strap does most of the work of keeping the shank locked to your leg. If it is loose or stretched, the climber rolls on the calf, the gaff kicks out of the bark and you burn energy fighting it on every step. A firm 26 inch leather strap cinched over a good pad keeps the shank in line so the gaff sets where you put it.

Leather breaks in and shapes to your leg over the first few days. Expect to take up a hole or two as it settles. Pair new uppers with fresh lower straps if those are worn too, and see the rest of our climbing spurs and parts for pads and gaffs.

Keep the leather clean and treat it with a leather conditioner now and then so it does not dry out and crack. Do not leave straps soaked in the truck or next to a heater. Check the buckle, keeper and stitching, and look for cracks or torn holes before each climb.

Spurs are for removals, not pruning live trees. Spur straps are part of your climbing system's footing, so replace them as soon as they are damaged, keep a lanyard around the stem at all times and follow ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions.

faq.q: Are these upper or lower straps?
faq.a: Upper. They go around the calf just below the knee. Lower straps go around the ankle and are sold separately.

faq.q: Will they fit spurs from other makers?
faq.a: Most standard spurs use similar upper strap slots, but check the strap width against your climbers before ordering.

name: 7/8" Mammoth Rigging Line
title: 7/8 Mammoth Rigging Line for Heavy Removals
meta: The 7/8 Mammoth rigging line is a heavy lowering rope for big wood and crane-free removals. When 7/8 inch makes sense, matching hardware and inspection tips.
tagline: A 7/8 in rigging line for the heaviest blocking and lowering work.
summary: The 7/8 Mammoth rigging line is the heaviest size in the line, built for crews that block down big trunk wood and lower heavy tops. It is more rope than most daily jobs need, which is exactly why it earns a spot on the truck for the big removals.
highlights: 7/8 in diameter for heavy rigging
Sized for big blocked-down wood and heavy tops
Needs blocks and lowering devices rated for 7/8 in rope
More strength margin than 5/8 or 3/4 in line
Heavier to carry, so plan the setup
specs: See the maker's rated breaking strength

p: Most crews rig with 1/2 or 5/8 inch line and step up as the wood gets bigger. A 7/8 inch line is for the top of that range: long blocked trunk sections, heavy leaders and big tops where the shock load at the catch is serious. The larger rope gives you more strength margin and holds up better to the wraps on a lowering device.

The cost is weight and bulk. A long hank of 7/8 is a real carry, so many crews keep it for the jobs that need it and run smaller line the rest of the time. Your block, sling and porta-wrap or bollard must all be rated for a 7/8 inch rope. Compare sizes in our rigging rope section.

Before and after each job, run the line through your hands. Look for cut or pulled strands, glazed or melted sections, flat spots and core damage. Keep it dry, out of the sun and away from fuel and bar oil.

Rigging forces are dynamic and can be several times the weight of the piece. Work from the maker's rated strength, allow for knots and bends, retire rope after a severe shock load and keep rigging to trained crews working under ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Is 7/8 inch rope overkill?
faq.a: For everyday pruning and small removals, usually. It is meant for heavy blocking and big pieces where a smaller line would be working near its limit.

faq.q: Will 7/8 inch fit my rigging block?
faq.a: Only if the block's sheave is rated for that diameter. Check the block maker's rope range before you rig.

name: Weaver Leather Cambium Friction Saver
title: Weaver Leather Cambium Friction Saver
meta: The Weaver leather cambium friction saver protects bark and your line at the tie-in point. How a ring-style cambium saver works, plus setup and inspection tips.
tagline: A ring-style cambium saver that protects bark and rope at your tie-in point.
summary: The Weaver leather cambium friction saver sits between your climbing line and the limb at your tie-in point, so the rope runs through rings instead of sawing across the bark. It protects the tree's cambium and saves wear on your rope on every climb.
highlights: Ring-style cambium saver for MRS/DdRT tie-ins
Protects bark and cambium at the crotch
Cuts rope wear and heat at the anchor
Retrievable from the ground with the right setup
Simple design that is easy to inspect

p: When you climb on a doubled rope over a limb, every advance drags the line across the bark. That burns the cambium, leaves a scar on the tree and glazes your rope. A cambium saver puts a strap and rings at the crotch so the rope runs through hardware instead. Climbing feels smoother, and the tree takes far less damage.

Ring-style savers like this one are simple and tough. Set it with a throw line, run your climbing line through both rings and tie in as usual. With a retrieval setup you can pull it down from the ground at the end of the job. Compare other friction savers if you want an adjustable model.
A cambium saver also cuts the heat and friction you feel when advancing your hitch, so long climbs to a high tie-in take less effort.

Install it so both rings sit on the same side of the limb and the rope runs through them in the direction the maker shows. Choose a sound crotch sized for the saver. Before each climb, check the strap and stitching for cuts, abrasion and heat damage, and the rings for grooves or sharp edges.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it aloft.

faq.q: Can I use it for SRS?
faq.a: A cambium saver is mainly used for MRS/DdRT climbing. Follow Weaver's instructions for any other use.

faq.q: How do I get it down?
faq.a: Most climbers retrieve it from the ground using the climbing line and a retrieval method suited to ring savers. Practice it low before relying on it.

name: ISC Chipmunk Flex Tether with Apex Rope Wrench
keyword: chipmunk flex tether with apex rope wrench
title: ISC Chipmunk Flex Tether with Apex Rope Wrench
h1: ISC Chipmunk Flex Tether with Apex Rope Wrench
meta: The ISC Chipmunk flex tether with Apex rope wrench pairs a rope wrench and tether for hitch-based SRS climbing. How it works, setup notes and inspection points.
tagline: A rope wrench and flexible tether combo for hitch-based SRS climbing.
summary: This ISC Chipmunk flex tether with Apex rope wrench pairs a rope wrench with ISC's flexible Chipmunk tether, the combination many climbers use to run a friction hitch on a stationary rope. The wrench adds the friction a hitch alone cannot give on a single line, and the tether keeps it aligned.
highlights: Rope wrench and flex tether in one combo
Adds friction so a hitch works on a single rope
Flexible tether keeps the wrench in line
Built for SRS work positioning and descent
Set up only as ISC shows

p: On a stationary rope, a friction hitch alone does not hold or descend smoothly because the rope does not double back on itself. A rope wrench solves that. The rope runs through the wrench above the hitch, adding friction, and the hitch does the gripping and tending. The flexible tether links the wrench to the hitch and keeps the two aligned as you move around the canopy.
Buying the wrench and tether together saves piecing it together and keeps the setup the way ISC tested it. Compare other SRS climbing devices if you prefer a mechanical device.

Many climbers like a wrench setup because it keeps the familiar feel of a hitch while working on a single rope. You can descend smoothly, stop anywhere and advance with a hitch tender, which makes long limb walks and redirects more manageable than on a doubled line.

Use rope diameters and hitch cord ISC lists for the wrench, and build the system exactly as the instructions show, with approved connectors. Test the setup on the ground and at low height before climbing. Before each climb, check the wrench for grooves and sharp edges, and the tether for cuts, fuzzing and stiffness.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it aloft.

faq.q: Do I need a hitch with a rope wrench?
faq.a: Yes. The wrench adds friction, but a friction hitch tied below it does the gripping. Use the hitch cord ISC recommends.

faq.q: Can I replace just the tether?
faq.a: Yes, the Chipmunk flex tether is available on its own. Replace it whenever it shows wear.

name: Retrieval Link for Friction Saver
title: Friction Saver Retrieval Link for Ring Savers
meta: A friction saver retrieval link helps pull a ring friction saver down from the ground after the climb. How it works, rigging it and why it is not life support.
tagline: A small link that makes pulling your friction saver down from the ground easier.
summary: A friction saver retrieval link clips to the small ring of a ring-style friction saver so you can pull it out of the tree from the ground. It is a small, cheap part that saves a climb back up or a saver left hanging in the crotch.
highlights: Helps retrieve a ring-style friction saver
Attaches at the small ring
Saves a climb back up to recover gear
Retrieval only, not load bearing

p: Ring friction savers are easy to set and hard to get down. Without help, pulling one out of a tight crotch often means the rings jam or the saver hangs up on bark. A retrieval link gives your retrieval line a clean point to pull from, so the small ring follows the big ring through and the saver drops out.

Set it up on the ground before you install the saver, and practice the retrieval low a few times so it is routine. Check that the link fits your saver's small ring. See more friction savers and parts.

A clean retrieval also protects the tree. Yanking on a stuck saver tears bark and can break small limbs, while a smooth pull lets the rings slide through the crotch without a fight. It saves the climber a trip back up and keeps the end of the day moving.

The link is a retrieval aid and never part of your climbing system. Do not clip a life-support line to it, and do not use it to connect anything you hang on. Before each job, check it for cracks, bending and sharp edges, and replace it if it is damaged.
Keep the friction saver itself on a normal inspection schedule. Climbing gear must meet the applicable standard, follow ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions, and be used by trained climbers.

faq.q: Can I climb on the retrieval link?
faq.a: No. It is only for pulling the saver down. Keep it out of the life-support path.

faq.q: Will it fit my friction saver?
faq.a: It suits common ring-style savers. Check the small ring size on your saver before ordering.

name: Kask Super Plasma Visor
title: Kask Super Plasma Visor for Climbing Helmets
meta: The Kask Super Plasma visor adds face and eye protection to your Kask helmet for cutting, chipping and grinding. Fit notes, care tips and when to replace it.
tagline: A helmet-mounted visor that adds face protection to the Kask Super Plasma.
summary: The Kask Super Plasma visor mounts to the front of the Kask Super Plasma helmet to shield your eyes and face from chips, sawdust and twigs. It flips up when you do not need it and drops into place when the saw starts.
highlights: Made for the Kask Super Plasma helmet
Shields eyes and face from chips and debris
Flips up out of the way between cuts
Replaces a scratched or cracked visor

p: Running a saw overhead sends a steady stream of chips at your face, and chipper and grinder work throws debris too. A visor mounted to the helmet stays with you as you move, flips up to read a cut or talk to the crew, and comes back down without hunting for glasses in a pocket.
Check the listing for which visor style this is and that it fits your helmet version, then compare it with the other eye protection we carry.

Grit and sawdust are not the only hazard. Twigs and small branches snap back at your face when you push through the canopy or drop a limb, and a visor takes that hit instead of your eyes. On a long day of trimming, being able to flip the visor down without stopping is what makes people actually use it. Keep a spare in the truck, since a badly scratched visor is hard to see through in low light.

Many climbers wear safety glasses under the visor, since a flipped-up visor protects nothing. Check the markings on the visor and your employer's rules to confirm it meets the eye protection standard required for your work.

Clean it with water and a soft cloth, not a dry rag, which scratches the surface. Replace the visor if it is cracked, deeply scratched or no longer stays in position. Inspect the helmet and its mounts at the same time, and follow ANSI Z133 and Kask's instructions.

faq.q: Will this visor fit other Kask helmets?
faq.a: It is made for the Super Plasma. Check Kask's compatibility list before fitting it to another model.

faq.q: Do I still need safety glasses?
faq.a: Wearing safety glasses under the visor is a common practice and may be required by your employer. Check your site rules.

name: Shembiner XL Chainsaw Hook
title: Shembiner XL Chainsaw Hook for Saddles
meta: The Shembiner XL chainsaw hook gives your climbing saw a dedicated spot on the saddle. How the XL size compares, where to mount it and why it is storage only.
tagline: A saddle hook in XL size that gives your climbing saw its own place to hang.
summary: The Shembiner XL chainsaw hook mounts on your saddle and gives a top-handle saw a dedicated place to hang between cuts. The XL size leaves room for larger saw lanyard rings and handles than the standard hook.
highlights: Dedicated saddle hook for a climbing saw
XL size for larger rings and handles
Quick one-handed clip between cuts
Keeps the saw off gear loops
Storage only, not life support

body.h: A better place for the saw
p: Hanging a top-handle saw from a general gear loop is awkward and wears the loop out. A Shembiner hook gives the saw its own spot, so you can park it with one hand and reach for the hand saw or adjust your lanyard without fumbling.
The XL is a good choice if your saw lanyard uses a larger ring or you hang the saw by the handle. If you need a different size, compare the rest of our saddle storage options.

Mount it on the side of the saddle where the saw hangs clear of your climbing line and lanyard and does not swing into your legs. Practice clipping it on the ground until it is automatic. Keep the saw on a saw lanyard as well, so a missed clip does not send it to the ground crew.
This hook is a storage accessory. Never use it for life support or rigging. Check it for cracks and wear, and use a chainsaw aloft only with training and in line with ANSI Z133.

Look the hook over when you inspect the rest of your saddle hardware. A bent or cracked hook can drop the saw without warning, and replacement is cheap compared to a damaged saw or an injury on the ground.

faq.q: What is the difference between the XL and XLS?
faq.a: They are different sizes in the Shembiner line. Check the listing dimensions against your saw lanyard ring before choosing.

faq.q: Do I still need a saw lanyard?
faq.a: Yes. The hook parks the saw, and the lanyard keeps it tied to you if it slips.

name: 2-in-1 Hi-Vee Replacement Lanyard
title: 2-in-1 Hi-Vee Replacement Lanyard Rope
meta: A Hi-Vee replacement lanyard for 2-in-1 setups. Swap worn rope and reuse your hardware. What to check before you rebuild, plus inspection and retirement tips.
tagline: Replacement Hi-Vee rope for a 2-in-1 adjustable positioning lanyard.
summary: This Hi-Vee replacement lanyard is the rope for a 2-in-1 adjustable lanyard, sold so you can replace a worn line and keep your adjuster and snaps. It is the cheaper fix when the rope is tired but the hardware still passes inspection.
highlights: Replacement rope for a 2-in-1 lanyard
Hi-Vee braided rope
Reuse hardware that passes inspection
Less money than a full kit

p: A 2-in-1 lanyard runs the tail back through the adjuster so the same rope gives you a flipline length and a shorter positioning length. The rope takes all the wear, especially where it runs through the adjuster and wraps the stem, so it usually goes long before the snaps and adjuster do.

Before you rebuild, check that the rope diameter matches your adjuster's rated range and that your snaps or carabiners still pass inspection. If any hardware is worn, replace it too. Complete builds are in our rope lanyards section.

Rebuilding also lets you change the length. If your old lanyard always felt a little short on big stems, or long enough to get in the way, a new rope is the time to fix it. Mark the date you put it in service on a tag or in your gear log.
Run the rope through your hands before every climb. Look for cuts, glazing, flat spots, pulled strands and damage near the eyes. Retire it after a shock load or any damage you cannot explain.

A rope lanyard is not cut resistant. Keep the saw away from it and use a wire-core flipline for heavy spar work. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it aloft.

faq.q: Does it come with snaps or an adjuster?
faq.a: No. It is the rope only. Reuse hardware that passes inspection or buy new pieces rated for the rope.

faq.q: How do I know the rope fits my adjuster?
faq.a: Check the adjuster maker's rated rope diameter range against the Hi-Vee rope size listed.

name: Arborist Shackle
title: Arborist Shackle for Rigging and Hardware
meta: A load-rated arborist shackle for joining slings, rings and blocks in tree rigging. How to pick the right size, set the pin correctly and inspect it before use.
tagline: A rated shackle for connecting slings, blocks and rings in rigging setups.
summary: An arborist shackle is a simple, strong connector for joining slings, rigging rings and blocks. It is a staple in the rigging bag for the times a carabiner is the wrong tool, such as heavy static connections and hardware that stays put for the whole job.
highlights: Strong metal connector for rigging
Joins slings, rings and blocks
Working load marked on the body
Compact and easy to stash in the bag
specs: See working load marked on the shackle

p: In rigging, a shackle is the go-to when you need a strong connection that will not be opened and closed all day. Use it to hang a block on a sling, join a ring to a sling eye or connect hardware on a speedline anchor. It has a lot of strength for its size.

Size it by the working load marked on the shackle, not by feel, and make sure the bow is wide enough for the sling or eye without pinching it. See other rings and rigging hardware for more connectors.

Keep a few sizes in the rigging bag. A small shackle handles light hardware on pruning jobs, while bigger removals call for a larger shackle that matches the block and sling you are using. Mixed sizes mean you are not tempted to use the wrong one because it is the only one on the truck.
Seat the pin fully and snug it. On a screw-pin shackle, check it during the job, since rope movement can back the pin out. Load the shackle in line with its body and avoid side loading.

Before each job, look for bending, a stretched bow, cracks, corrosion and damaged threads, and retire any shackle that has been overloaded or will not close cleanly. Rigging gear is not for life support. Follow ANSI Z133 and the maker's ratings, and keep rigging to trained crews.

faq.q: Can I use a shackle in my climbing system?
faq.a: Only if it is specifically rated and approved for life support. A rigging shackle is for moving wood.

faq.q: How tight should the pin be?
faq.a: Snug by hand, fully seated, and checked during the job. Do not overtighten with a wrench unless the maker calls for it.

name: Best Practices for Safety in Arboriculture
keyword: best practices for safety in arboriculture
title: Best Practices for Safety in Arboriculture
h1: Best Practices for Safety in Arboriculture
meta: Best Practices for Safety in Arboriculture is a safety reference for tree crews. Who it suits, how to use it for training and how it ties back to ANSI Z133.
tagline: A safety reference for tree crews, foremen and anyone training new climbers.
summary: Best Practices for Safety in Arboriculture is a reference for tree workers who want the safety side of the job laid out in one place. It suits new crew members learning the basics and foremen looking for material to anchor tailgate meetings.
highlights: Safety-focused guide for tree care work
Useful for new climbers and ground workers
Good backing for tailgate safety meetings
Pairs with ANSI Z133 and hands-on training

p: Most accidents in tree work come back to the same handful of causes: electrical contact, falls, struck-by incidents and chainsaw cuts. A best-practices guide gives a crew a shared way to talk about those hazards, plan the work and set up the drop zone before anyone starts the saw.

It is useful for a new ground worker learning the job, a climber studying for a credential or a foreman planning safety meetings. Read a section, then talk it through on the job site with the crew. Browse more books and training materials for rigging and climbing titles.

A book does not replace training. Use it alongside ANSI Z133, your company's written procedures and hands-on instruction from a qualified trainer. Check the edition date and compare it with the current version of the standard, since practices change over time.
Keep a copy in the truck or crew room, and come back to it when a near miss or a new job type raises questions.

The best way to use it is in short pieces. Pick one topic each week, such as work zone setup, aerial rescue readiness or electrical hazard awareness, and spend ten minutes on it before the first cut of the day. Ask the newest person on the crew to explain it back. That kind of steady review builds habits that hold up when the job gets busy or the weather turns.

faq.q: Does this book replace ANSI Z133?
faq.a: No. Use it alongside the current standard and your company's procedures.

faq.q: Is it suitable for beginners?
faq.a: Yes. It works for new crew members as well as experienced workers refreshing the basics.

name: Notch Throwline Pop Box
title: Notch Throwline Pop Box for Throw Line Storage
meta: The Notch throwline pop box is a collapsible cube that holds throw line ready to feed out without tangles. How to pack it, use it and keep it clean on the job.
tagline: A collapsible cube that keeps throw line ready to throw without tangles.
summary: The Notch throwline pop box is a collapsible storage cube for throw line. It pops open on the ground so your line feeds out cleanly on each throw, then folds flat for the gear bag when the climbing line is set.
highlights: Collapsible cube for throw line
Line feeds out cleanly when you throw
Folds flat for storage
Keeps line off wet ground and debris

body.h: Why use a throw line cube
p: Throw line tangles easily. Left in a pile on the ground it catches on twigs, picks up grit and knots itself just as the bag is going up. A pop box gives the line a clean home. Stuff it in loosely after each throw and it pays out smoothly the next time.
The box also keeps line off wet grass and out of sawdust, which helps it run through the canopy and last longer. See our throw weights and line for line, bags and kits.

A cube also speeds up repeat throws. When the bag misses the target crotch, you pull the line back into the box and throw again without stopping to untangle a bird's nest at your feet. Over a day of setting lines in several trees, that time adds up, and the climber gets in the tree faster.

Feed the line in loosely by hand rather than coiling it, so it comes out without twists. Keep the end tied to a loop in the box so the whole line cannot fly out with the bag. Shake out bark and leaves at the end of the day and let it dry if it gets wet.
Stand clear of the throw path and look out for the bag on the way down. Never throw near power lines.

faq.q: Can I store two throw lines in it?
faq.a: It is best used with one line at a time so the lines do not tangle with each other.

faq.q: Does it come with throw line?
faq.a: Plan on adding your own throw line and bag unless the listing says otherwise.

name: Arborwear Trucker Patch Cap
title: Arborwear Trucker Patch Cap
meta: The Arborwear trucker patch cap pairs a mesh back with a front logo patch. A breathable cap for ground days, drive time and off-hours wear. Fit and care notes.
tagline: A mesh-back trucker cap with an Arborwear patch for ground days and drive time.
summary: The Arborwear trucker patch cap is a classic mesh-back trucker hat with an Arborwear logo patch on the front. It is the cap for ground work, drive time between jobs and the end of the day when the helmet comes off.
highlights: Classic trucker shape with a mesh back
Arborwear logo patch on the front
Adjustable snap back
Breathes well in warm weather

body.h: A cap for the in-between hours
p: Tree work runs on a helmet, but there are plenty of hours when you are not wearing one: driving to the job, writing estimates, fueling saws and grabbing lunch. A trucker cap keeps the sun out of your eyes and the sawdust out of your hair, and the mesh back lets heat out on hot days.
The patch front gives it a clean, simple look. Browse the rest of our hats and caps for other styles and colors.

Arborwear builds its clothing around tree work, and the cap fits that look. It pairs well with work pants and a hoodie on cold mornings and still breathes in the afternoon heat. Keep one in the truck for the drive between jobs, for a stop at the supply house, or for the days you are running the chipper or the stump grinder well away from overhead work. A light color stays cooler in direct sun, while a darker one hides bar oil and sap.

body.h: Fit, care and where not to wear it
p: The snap back adjusts to most heads. Hand wash in cool water and let it air dry so the brim keeps its shape.

A cap is not head protection. Wear a helmet that meets the required standard any time you are climbing, in a bucket or on the ground in the drop zone, and keep the cap for the times you are clear of overhead work.

faq.q: Is the cap adjustable?
faq.a: Yes, it uses an adjustable snap back.

faq.q: Can I wear it under a helmet?
faq.a: No. A cap brim interferes with helmet fit. Wear the helmet on its own as the maker intends.

name: Marvin Cast Saw Head with Adapter
keyword: marvin cast saw head with adapter
title: Marvin Cast Saw Head with Adapter
h1: Marvin Cast Saw Head with Adapter
meta: The Marvin cast saw head with adapter mounts a pole saw blade on your pole. Why the adapter matters, how to fit it to your pole, and care tips for long service.
tagline: A cast pole saw head with an adapter for mounting it to your pole.
summary: The Marvin cast saw head with adapter holds a pruning blade on the end of a pole, with the adapter that joins the head to the pole itself. It is the part to buy when you are building a pole saw or the old head and fitting are both worn out.
highlights: Cast pole saw head
Adapter included for mounting to the pole
Holds the blade solid in the cut
Rebuilds or upgrades an existing pole saw

p: A saw head on its own needs a matching fitting on the pole. The adapter version gives you that connection in the same purchase, which helps if you are building a pole saw from a bare pole or replacing a head that came off with a damaged fitting.

Check that the adapter matches your pole's size and type before you order, since makers use different fittings. Our pole saws and scabbards section has blades and complete saws if you need more parts.

A solid head matters most at full extension. Any play at the joint is multiplied at the end of a long pole, so the blade wobbles and the cut wanders. A fresh head and adapter take that slop out, and your cuts are easier to start and finish cleanly.

Mount the adapter securely and attach the blade with the teeth facing back so it cuts on the pull. Tighten everything until there is no play, then check it again after the first few cuts. A loose blade binds and wanders, which makes clean cuts at the branch collar hard.

Wipe sap off after use and keep the blade guarded in storage. Replace the head if the casting cracks or the blade seat wears. Never use a pole tool near energized lines unless you are a qualified line-clearance arborist with rated equipment.

faq.q: Does it include a blade?
faq.a: Plan on supplying your own pole saw blade unless the listing says one is included.

faq.q: Will the adapter fit any pole?
faq.a: No. Confirm that it matches your pole's size and fitting before ordering.

name: Petzl Delta Link
title: Petzl Delta Link: Steel Delta Quick Link
meta: The Petzl Delta link is a triangular steel quick link for closing harnesses and joining hardware for good. Where arborists use it and how to close and check it.
tagline: A triangular steel quick link for semi-permanent connections.
summary: The Petzl Delta link is a triangular steel quick link, often called a maillon, for connections that stay closed for long periods. Arborists use it to join hardware for good, such as attaching devices to a saddle bridge or closing a harness attachment point where the maker allows it.
highlights: Delta (triangle) shape spreads three-way loads
Steel for strength and wear resistance
Threaded sleeve closure
For semi-permanent connections
Ratings marked on the link

body.h: When a quick link beats a carabiner
p: A carabiner is made to be opened and closed all day. A quick link is the opposite: you close it once and leave it, which makes it ideal for gear that should stay put. The delta shape keeps a three-way load centered in the link, which suits closing a harness or holding a device and a tether together.
Check Petzl's ratings and your saddle maker's instructions to confirm a Delta is approved for the connection you plan to use it on. See more climbing hardware for rings and connectors.
Steel is heavier than aluminum but resists wear far better, which matters on a connection where a rope or another piece of hardware rubs all day.

Screw the sleeve fully closed and snug it. A quick link is only rated when the sleeve is closed. Check it during the day, as vibration can work it open, and some climbers close it with a wrench where the maker allows.

Inspect before every climb for corrosion, cracks, bending and damaged threads, and retire it after a big fall or if the sleeve will not turn smoothly. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it aloft.

faq.q: Is the Petzl Delta strong with the sleeve open?
faq.a: No. Its rating applies only with the sleeve fully closed. Never load it open.

faq.q: Can I use it in place of a locking carabiner?
faq.a: Only for connections meant to stay closed and where your gear's maker approves it. It is not for clipping in and out.

name: 3/4" Ring Sling with Beast Ring
title: 3/4" Ring Sling with Beast Ring for Rigging
meta: A 3/4 inch ring sling with Beast ring makes a smooth, heavy-duty friction rigging point for big removals. Sizing notes, setup and inspection advice for crews.
tagline: A 3/4 in rope sling with a large Beast ring for heavy friction rigging.
summary: This 3/4 inch ring sling with Beast ring gives you a heavy-duty rigging point that is lighter than a big block. Choke the sling on the stem and run your rigging line over the large ring for friction, or clip a block to it.
highlights: 3/4 in rope sling for heavy rigging
Large Beast ring for a broad rope path
Builds useful friction at the top
Lighter to carry than a big steel block
specs: See sling tag and ring markings

p: A large rigging ring lets the rope bend over a wide radius, which is easier on the line than a small ring and adds friction at the top. That friction takes some load off the lowering device and helps control big pieces. A 3/4 inch sling suits the heavy end of the work, where the rigging point has to carry large wood.
Match the sling and ring rating to your rigging line and the loads you plan to catch. Compare other heavy-duty slings for different lengths and ends.

Rings also make rigging quicker to set. There is no sheave to line up and nothing to jam, so the climber can hang the sling, run the line and get back to cutting. When the job calls for repeated heavy lowering with less friction, clip a block to the ring instead. Choose a sling length that lets you choke the stem with the ring sitting where the rope will run cleanly.

Before each job, check the sling for cut or pulled strands, glazing, stiff spots and intact splices, and check the ring for grooves, gouges and sharp edges. Retire anything damaged or shock loaded beyond plan.
Rigging forces can be several times the weight of the piece. Use the maker's ratings, follow ANSI Z133 and keep rigging work to trained crews. Rigging gear is never used for life support.

faq.q: Can a ring replace a block?
faq.a: For some work. A ring adds friction and saves weight, while a block runs freer for repeated heavy lowering.

faq.q: Is 3/4 inch more sling than I need?
faq.a: For everyday pruning rigging, often. It is meant for heavy removal work and big wood.

name: Weaver WLC-330 Arborist Saddle
title: Weaver WLC-330 Arborist Saddle
meta: The Weaver WLC-330 arborist saddle is a working saddle from Weaver Leather's WLC line. Who it suits, fitting advice and daily checks to make before you climb.
tagline: A Weaver Leather arborist saddle for working climbers.
summary: The Weaver WLC-330 arborist saddle is part of Weaver Leather's WLC line of tree climbing saddles. It suits climbers who want a straightforward, durable Weaver saddle for pruning and removals. Check Weaver's current spec sheet for exact sizing and attachment points before buying.
highlights: Weaver Leather WLC series saddle
Built for pruning and removal work
Side D-rings for lanyard positioning
Sized fit for a secure, level hang

p: Weaver's WLC saddles run from basic models to fully featured ones. The WLC-330 is a working saddle for climbers who want something tough enough for spur work, bark and grit without paying for features they will not use. Side D-rings take a lanyard or flipline for positioning.
Comfort depends on how you climb. If you spend long hours sitting in the saddle, compare padding and attachment layouts in our Weaver saddles section and pick the one that fits your work.

A working saddle like the WLC-330 is also a sensible choice as a second saddle on the truck or as a first saddle for a new climber who is still learning what features matter. Whoever wears it, take time to adjust it properly before the first climb and recheck the fit after a few days of use, once the materials settle.

Fit the saddle with Weaver's sizing guide. It should sit snug on the hips with the leg straps set so you hang level. Confirm which attachment points are approved for your climbing system before setting it up.

Inspect before every climb: webbing, leather, stitching, buckles and D-rings. Retire the saddle if you find cuts, heat damage, cracks or distortion. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it aloft.

faq.q: Is the WLC-330 good for a beginner?
faq.a: It can be. Fit and training matter more than the model. Get properly fitted and learn your system with a qualified trainer.

faq.q: Can I use it for SRS?
faq.a: Check Weaver's instructions for approved attachment points and configurations before using it with any system.

name: Weaver Arborist Doctor-Style Canvas Tool Bag
title: Weaver Doctor-Style Canvas Tool Bag for Arborists
h1: Weaver Arborist Doctor-Style Canvas Tool Bag
meta: The Weaver doctor-style canvas tool bag opens wide so gear and hand tools are easy to see and grab. What fits, how crews use it and how to keep it clean.
tagline: A wide-mouth canvas tool bag that keeps climbing gear and hand tools in reach.
summary: The Weaver doctor-style canvas tool bag opens wide at the top like an old doctor's bag, so you can see and grab gear without digging. It is a tidy home for hardware, hitch cords, files and hand tools on the truck and at the base of the tree.
highlights: Doctor-style wide-mouth opening
Tough canvas construction
Holds hardware, cords and hand tools
Stands open at the base of the tree

p: Most gear bags make you dig. A doctor-style bag opens wide at the top and stays open, so you can see every carabiner, hitch cord and file at a glance. Set it at the base of the tree and the ground crew can find what the climber is asking for without dumping the bag in the dirt.
Canvas is tough and handles bark, sap and the truck bed well. Compare other gear bags if you need a bigger bag or a rope bag.

A lot of climbers keep one bag for the climbing kit and a second for small tools, so nothing gets mixed up. Throw in a spare hitch cord, a few locking carabiners, a pulley, files, a scrench and a roll of tape, and you have a quick-grab kit that lives on the truck. The handles make it easy to carry from the truck to the tree in one trip, and the open top means the climber's requests can be filled fast. It also keeps small parts from getting lost in the bed of the truck.

Keep life-support gear separate from fuel, bar oil and sharp tools. Fuel and oil can damage textiles, and loose saw files or blades can cut rope and slings. Small pouches or a divider help keep hardware organized.
Brush off sawdust and let the bag dry if it gets wet before closing it up. A dry, clean bag keeps your soft goods in better condition between jobs.

faq.q: Can I store rope in it?
faq.a: Short hitch cords and lanyards fit fine. A full climbing line is better in a dedicated rope bag.

faq.q: Is canvas waterproof?
faq.a: Canvas sheds light rain but is not waterproof. Dry the bag and its contents after wet days.

name: Replacement Speed Line Bale
title: Replacement Speed Line Bale
meta: A replacement speed line bale for a speedline kit. Swap a worn or bent bale so loads run cleanly down the line. Fit checks, inspection and when to retire it.
tagline: A replacement bale for keeping your speedline kit in working order.
summary: This replacement speed line bale is a spare part for a speedline kit, the setup crews use to zip brush and light wood from the tree to the drop zone. A worn or bent bale makes the load hang badly on the line, so replacing it keeps the kit running smoothly.
highlights: Spare part for a speedline kit
Replaces a worn, bent or lost bale
Keeps loads tracking cleanly down the line
Cheaper than replacing the whole kit
specs: Speedline brush and light wood removal

p: A speedline moves brush and small wood along a tensioned line from the canopy to a landing zone, saving the ground crew a lot of dragging. Every part takes wear, and a bale that is bent, grooved or lost will make loads hang crooked or bind on the line.
Check that this bale matches your kit before you order, since speedline parts vary by maker. Our rigging kits section has complete speedline kits if you need more than one part.

Keeping spare parts on the truck means one damaged piece does not end the speedline for the day. Many crews keep a small parts kit with the speedline gear: a spare bale, connectors and slings, so a quick swap keeps the brush moving. Check the bale's fit on the trolley or pulley before you tension the line, since a part that seats poorly will show up as a load that swings or hangs up halfway down. It is a small part, but it decides how well everything else works together.
Inspect the bale before each use for bending, cracks, sharp edges and wear grooves. Retire it if it is deformed or no longer sits right on the hardware.

Keep the speedline loads light, keep the landing zone clear and make sure the line is anchored and tensioned according to the kit's instructions. Speedline gear is for moving wood, never for life support. Follow ANSI Z133 and train the crew before using it.

faq.q: Will this bale fit my speedline kit?
faq.a: Check your kit's maker and part details against the listing. Parts are not always interchangeable between kits.

faq.q: What loads can a speedline carry?
faq.a: Brush and light wood. Follow the kit's ratings and keep loads within them.

name: Teufelberger Tachyon Ash Lanyard Kit
title: Tachyon Ash Lanyard Kit for Tree Climbers
meta: The Tachyon ash lanyard kit is built on Teufelberger tachyon rope in ash for work positioning. What a kit covers, how climbers use it and how to inspect it.
tagline: A positioning lanyard kit built on Teufelberger tachyon rope in ash.
summary: The Tachyon ash lanyard kit puts Teufelberger's tachyon climbing rope, in its ash colorway, together with the parts for an adjustable positioning lanyard. It gives you a second point of attachment so you can lean back and work with both hands.
highlights: Built on Teufelberger tachyon rope
Ash colorway, a subdued tone
Adjustable work-positioning lanyard
Tachyon holds hitches and runs through adjusters smoothly
Kit saves sourcing parts separately

p: A positioning lanyard wraps the stem or a limb and holds you in place while you cut, flip up a spar or reposition. Snug the adjuster, lean back and you have both hands free for the saw.

Tachyon is a firm 11.5 mm rope that grips well under a hitch and feeds smoothly through mechanical adjusters. The ash color is quieter than the bright options, which some climbers prefer. Read the listing for the length and adjuster type, and see all our lanyard kits to compare.

Confirm every part is assembled as the maker specifies and that the adjuster is rated for the rope diameter. Inspect the rope, eyes and hardware before every climb, and retire it after a cut, glazing, a shock load or any damage you cannot explain.

A rope lanyard is not cut resistant, so keep the saw away from it and use a wire-core flipline for heavy spar work. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it aloft.
Keep a record of when the lanyard went into service so you can track its age along with your climbing line.

faq.q: Does the ash color perform differently?
faq.a: No. Color is about visibility and preference. Performance is the same tachyon rope.

faq.q: Can I replace just the rope later?
faq.a: Yes. Replacement tachyon lanyard rope is available, so you can keep hardware that still passes inspection.

name: Yale 10mm Beeline Split Tail
title: Yale 10mm Beeline Split Tail Hitch Cord
meta: The Yale 10mm Beeline split tail is a polyester hitch cord for friction hitch systems. Why climbers like Beeline, how to tie it in and when to retire it.
tagline: A 10 mm Beeline hitch cord with an eye for tying a split tail system.
summary: The Yale 10mm Beeline split tail is a length of Yale's Beeline polyester hitch cord made up as a split tail, the separate cord climbers use to tie a friction hitch onto their climbing line. Beeline is known for holding a hitch firmly and handling heat well.
highlights: 10 mm Yale Beeline hitch cord
Made up as a split tail
Holds a friction hitch firmly
Polyester construction handles heat well
Replace it often, as hitch cord is a wear item

p: A split tail separates the hitch from the climbing line. Instead of tying the hitch with the rope's own tail, you tie it with a dedicated cord. When the hitch cord wears, you replace a short, cheap piece instead of cutting the end off your climbing rope.
A 10 mm Beeline cord suits common 11 to 13 mm climbing lines, but always test the hitch on your actual rope before climbing on it. See more hitch cord and split tails for other sizes and makers.

Beeline is made for hitch work and is known for handling the heat of long descents, so it stays consistent where cheaper cord can glaze. Many climbers keep two or three split tails in the bag so a worn one can be swapped mid-job.

Hitch cord takes heat and wear on every descent. Check it before each climb for glazing, stiffness, fuzzing, cover damage and wear at the eye, and retire it early. Many climbers replace hitch cord much sooner than any other soft good.

Dress and set the hitch carefully and test it on the ground before leaving it. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it aloft.

faq.q: What hitch should I tie?
faq.a: Common choices are the Distel, Valdotain tresse and similar hitches. Learn and test them under a qualified trainer.

faq.q: Will 10 mm grip on my rope?
faq.a: It depends on your rope's diameter and cover. Test it on your line at ground level first.

name: D-Shaped Locksafe Carabiner with ANSI Gate
title: D-Shaped Locksafe Carabiner with ANSI Gate
h1: D-Shaped Locksafe Carabiner with ANSI Gate
meta: A D-shaped Locksafe carabiner with a high-strength ANSI gate for climbing systems. Where the D shape helps, how the auto-lock works and how to inspect it.
tagline: An auto-locking D carabiner with a high-strength gate for climbing systems.
summary: This D-shaped Locksafe carabiner pairs DMM's Locksafe auto-locking gate with a gate built to ANSI gate-strength requirements. The D shape puts the load near the spine, where the carabiner is strongest.
highlights: D shape keeps the load near the spine
Locksafe auto-locking gate
Gate made for ANSI gate-strength requirements
For connections in arborist climbing systems
Ratings marked on the spine

p: Arborist systems load connectors in ways sport climbing does not, with gates pressed against stems, hardware and rope. A high-strength gate gives more margin if the gate itself is loaded. Check the markings on the carabiner to confirm the gate rating, and make sure it suits the standard your work requires.

A D shape is a good general choice for lanyard ends, saddle bridges and device connections. Locksafe gates lock automatically and take a deliberate twist-and-pull to open. See other auto-locking carabiners to compare shapes.

Keep connectors in your climbing system separate from rigging hardware. A carabiner that has been used to move wood may have taken loads or damage you cannot see, and it should not go back on your saddle.

Load the carabiner along its spine, keep the gate closed and locked, and watch for cross-loading against other hardware. Before every climb, check that the gate closes and locks fully on its own, and look for grooves, sharp edges, cracks and corrosion. Retire it after a big fall or a drop onto a hard surface.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it aloft.

faq.q: What does ANSI gate mean?
faq.a: It refers to a gate built to meet ANSI gate-strength requirements. Confirm the rating stamped on the carabiner before use.

faq.q: How does a Locksafe gate open?
faq.a: Twist the sleeve and pull it down, then open the gate. It relocks on its own when released.

name: DMM Shadow Carabiner, Matt Gray
title: DMM Shadow Carabiner, Matt Gray
meta: The DMM Shadow carabiner in matt gray is an aluminum auto-locking carabiner for arborist climbing connections. Gate, finish and inspection notes in one page.
tagline: An aluminum auto-locking carabiner in a low-glare matt gray finish.
summary: The DMM Shadow carabiner in matt gray is an aluminum auto-locking carabiner with a keylock nose that does not snag on rope or slings. The matt gray finish has a low-glare, understated look that many climbers like.
highlights: Aluminum auto-locking carabiner
Keylock nose that will not snag
Matt gray, low-glare finish
Made in Wales by DMM
Ratings marked on the spine

p: The Shadow is a general-purpose connector for arborist work: lanyard ends, connecting devices and clipping to saddle attachment points. The keylock nose runs smoothly through rope eyes and sling loops without hooking, which saves frustration when you are clipping in one-handed.
The matt gray finish is about looks, not performance. It is the same Shadow, just in a muted color. Compare other auto-locking carabiners if you need a different shape or gate.

Some climbers use color to organize their saddle, with one color for the climbing system and another for lanyards or spare connectors. A matt gray carabiner stands out from the bright anodized colors many arborist connectors come in, so it is easy to set aside for one job. It also shows fewer scuffs from bark and grit than a glossy finish. Whatever system you use, keep it consistent so you can find the right carabiner by feel and sight while working aloft.

Load it along the spine with the gate closed and locked. Before each climb, check that the gate snaps shut and locks on its own, and look for grooves, cracks, sharp edges and corrosion. Retire it after a big fall or a drop onto a hard surface.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it aloft.

faq.q: Does the matt gray finish change the strength?
faq.a: No. Ratings are marked on the spine and are the same as for other Shadow colors.

faq.q: Is the Shadow good for rigging?
faq.a: It is a climbing connector. Use rigging hardware rated for the load when moving wood.

name: Teufelberger 10mm Ocean Polyester Split Tail
title: Teufelberger 10mm Ocean Polyester Split Tail
meta: The Teufelberger 10mm Ocean Polyester split tail is a hitch cord for friction hitch climbing systems. Why climbers use it, tying tips and when to replace it.
tagline: A 10 mm Ocean Polyester hitch cord made up as a split tail.
summary: The Teufelberger 10mm Ocean Polyester split tail is a hitch cord made from Ocean Polyester, set up as a split tail for tying a friction hitch on your climbing line. It is a long-running favorite for climbers who want a firm, predictable hitch.
highlights: 10 mm Ocean Polyester hitch cord
Split tail for friction hitch systems
Polyester handles heat on descents
Predictable grip on common climbing lines

p: Ocean Polyester has been used as hitch cord for years because it grabs consistently and holds up to heat on long descents. In a split tail system it is tied onto the climbing line as a separate hitch, so when it wears out you replace a short piece of cord rather than cutting your rope.

Ten millimeter cord suits many common climbing lines, but grip changes with rope diameter and cover, so test the hitch on your own line before you leave the ground. See more hitch cord and split tails to compare.

Keep a spare split tail in your gear bag. A worn hitch cord is a reason to swap it on the spot, and having one ready means you do not have to cut the day short or climb on a cord you are not happy with.
Check the cord before every climb for glazing, stiffness, fuzzing, cuts and wear at the eye, and retire it early. Hitch cord is the fastest-wearing soft good in your system.

Dress and set the hitch carefully and use a micro pulley or hitch tender if your system calls for one. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it aloft.

faq.q: How long should a split tail last?
faq.a: It depends on how much you climb and descend. Inspect it every day and retire it at the first sign of glazing or damage.

faq.q: Can I use it on a 13 mm rope?
faq.a: Test the hitch on your rope at ground level first, since grip varies with rope diameter and cover.

name: Edelrid Flex Pro II Harness
title: Edelrid Flex Pro II Harness: Full Body Fall Protection
meta: The Edelrid Flex Pro II harness is a full body harness for work at height and fall protection. Who it suits, fitting advice and the checks to make before use.
tagline: A full body harness from Edelrid for work at height and fall protection.
summary: The Edelrid Flex Pro II harness is a full body harness for work at height, built for workers who need fall arrest attachment and comfort for long shifts. Tree crews use full body harnesses in aerial lifts and for other at-height work.
highlights: Full body harness for work at height
Fall arrest attachment point
Adjustable fit for long shifts
From Edelrid, a German maker of climbing and safety gear

body.h: Where a full body harness fits
p: A tree climbing saddle is built for work positioning in the canopy. A full body harness is built for fall arrest, with an attachment point between the shoulder blades that keeps you upright if you fall. Tree crews most often need one in bucket trucks and aerial lifts, where many employers and lift makers call for full body fall protection.
Check the label and Edelrid's documentation for the standards it is certified to and the attachment points approved for each use. See more fall protection gear for lanyards and connectors.

Comfort matters more than people think with a full body harness. In a bucket, you may wear it all day, and a harness that rubs or rides up gets loosened or left off. Padding, adjustable shoulder and leg straps and a good fit make it easier to wear correctly for a full shift. Try it on with the clothing you work in.
Fit it with all straps snug and the back attachment centered between the shoulder blades. Leg straps should be tight enough that a flat hand fits underneath but not a fist.

Inspect before every use for cut or frayed webbing, damaged stitching, cracked buckles and bent hardware, and retire it after any fall arrest. Fall protection gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the maker's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be used only by trained workers.

faq.q: Can I use a full body harness for tree climbing?
faq.a: It is built for fall arrest, not canopy work positioning. Use a tree climbing saddle for climbing unless the maker approves the harness for it.

faq.q: Do I need one in a bucket truck?
faq.a: Many employers and lift makers require full body fall protection in aerial lifts. Follow your lift's instructions and company rules.

name: Arbonaut Pink and Blue 11.5mm Climbing Rope
keyword: arbonaut pink and blue 11.5mm climbing rope
title: Arbonaut Pink and Blue 11.5mm Climbing Rope
h1: Arbonaut Pink and Blue 11.5mm Climbing Rope
meta: The Arbonaut pink and blue 11.5mm climbing rope is a tree line for MRS and SRS work. How 11.5 mm handles with hitches and devices, plus inspection tips.
tagline: An 11.5 mm tree climbing line in a bright pink and blue pattern.
summary: The Arbonaut pink and blue 11.5mm climbing rope is a tree climbing line in a mid-range diameter that works for both moving rope and stationary rope systems. The bright pink and blue pattern is easy to spot in the canopy and easy to tell apart from rigging line.
highlights: 11.5 mm tree climbing rope
Pink and blue pattern for visibility
Mid-range diameter for hitches and devices
Suits MRS and SRS where devices allow

p: An 11.5 mm line sits in the middle of the arborist range. It is thick enough to grip in the hand and hold a friction hitch well, and slim enough to run through most mechanical devices and pulleys. That makes it a practical do-everything rope if you climb both moving rope and stationary rope.
Always check that your hitch cord, pulley and any device are rated for an 11.5 mm rope before you climb, and test the hitch on the ground. Compare other climbing ropes in this section.

The bright pattern helps the ground crew. They can follow your line through the canopy, see where it runs over limbs and tell at a glance which rope is yours when several lines are in the tree. It also makes it harder to grab the climbing line by mistake when bagging rigging rope at the end of the job.

Keep the rope in a bag, away from fuel, bar oil, sunlight and the saw. Inspect it before every climb, along the full length, for cuts, glazing, flat spots, cover damage and core showing. Retire it after a severe shock load or any damage you cannot explain.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it aloft.

faq.q: Can I use this rope for rigging?
faq.a: No. Keep climbing rope for climbing only, and use a dedicated rigging line for moving wood.

faq.q: Will it work with my SRS device?
faq.a: Check the device maker's approved rope range and list before using any rope with it.

name: Yale Phantom Lanyard (Green and Purple, No Hardware)
title: Yale Phantom Lanyard, Green and Purple (No Hardware)
h1: Yale Phantom Lanyard, Green and Purple, Without Hardware
meta: The Yale Phantom lanyard in green and purple, sold without hardware so you can build it with your own adjuster and connectors. Setup tips and inspection points.
tagline: A green and purple rope lanyard sold bare so you can set it up your way.
summary: The Yale Phantom lanyard in green and purple comes without hardware, so you choose the adjuster and connectors that suit how you climb. The green and purple pattern stands apart from your climbing line and from other crew members' gear.
highlights: Sold without hardware for a custom build
Green and purple colorway
Works with a mechanical adjuster or a friction hitch
Rope lanyard for positioning

p: Buying a lanyard bare makes sense when you already have an adjuster you trust, or you want your connectors to match the rest of your saddle. Most climbers set it up as a 2-in-1 or a standard positioning lanyard with an adjuster and a locking connector at each end.

Match the adjuster to the rope diameter its maker lists, and make sure the eyes seat on your carabiners without side-loading the gate. If you would rather buy it ready to go, see our complete fliplines and lanyards.

Bright two-tone rope also helps on busy jobs. The ground crew can see which line is your lanyard at a glance, and you are less likely to grab the wrong tail when you are tired. Record the date it went into service so you know its age when inspection time comes around.
Keep the lanyard snug and above the saw's path, and never cut toward it. A rope lanyard is not cut resistant, so use a wire-core flipline for heavy spar work.

Check it before every climb for cuts, glazing, flat spots and eye damage, and retire it after a shock load. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard, be used per the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and be inspected before every climb. Get trained before you rely on it aloft.

faq.q: What hardware do I need?
faq.a: A locking carabiner or snap at each end and an adjuster or friction hitch, all rated for life support and for the rope diameter.

faq.q: Is the green and purple the same rope as the pink and black?
faq.a: Yes, it is the same Phantom rope. Only the color differs.
